rows.description: A student sets a time limit, submits a solid version and notes what to improve next time; aiming for excellence with flexibility keeps the gains of high standards without the paralysis.

rows.description: An adult polishes every report and delays delivery, while colleagues take the credit for speed; high standards help, but rigid ones cost time, rest and relationships.

rows.description: A friend notices someone cancel plans and lose sleep over tiny flaws in their work and offers to review it as a good enough draft; company can make imperfection feel survivable.

rows.description: A teenager who said something awkward at a party replays it for days and imagines everyone still thinking of it; repetition feels like problem solving but deepens the sting.

rows.description: A student who failed a paper asks over and over why it happened and what it says about them without arriving at any plan; thinking about causes without action keeps the mood low.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A friend who keeps rehashing a disappointment with the same person notices the talk gives no relief; the friend gently asks what small step might help now.

rows.description: An adult who notices they are ruminating writes the thought down, sets a short time for it and then does something absorbing such as walking or cooking; if it becomes constant or dark, professional help is wise.

rows.description: A child lying in bed wonders what if they fail or something happens to their mother; worry tries to prepare for danger but mostly manufactures alarms, and a calm routine and reassurance help.

rows.description: A teenager thinks of every possible way an exam could go wrong and can barely start studying; worry feels like responsibility, though it often replaces action.
